steps.message:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station Ulakwo, Etche LGA**

The VES interpretation at Ulakwo reveals a four-layer subsurface sequence. Layer 1 is a thin topsoil/lateritic unit (14.4 Ω·m, 0.12 m thick), underlain by Layer 2, a slightly more resistive sandy/clayey horizon (16.0 Ω·m, 8.25 m thick, base at 9.67 m). Layer 3 is a markedly resistive formation (4591.4 Ω·m, 27.07 m thick, base at 47.74 m), likely coarse sand or gravel, and the sequence terminates in Layer 4, the most resistive basal unit (5101.5 Ω·m), interpreted as the main aquiferous/bedrock zone.

Resistivities increase progressively with depth (r1 < r2 < r3 < r4), consistent with a continuously ascending curve. Both three-layer segments (1-2-3 and 2-3-4) satisfy the A-type condition, confirming the station's filed classification as A-type is appropriate.
